_note: Standalone model (Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Ltd = the lead-acid business, lubes and a little lithium trading), the basis the street uses for the core (MOFSL, Nuvama, Anand Rathi, 360 ONE, ICICI Direct and Avendus value standalone FY28E EPS). The lithium-ion subsidiary ARACT and the other subsidiaries (ARCSPL recycling, ARPSL, ARBME) are valued separately in the sum of the parts. FY26 base = Screener standalone (revenue Rs13,549 cr, EBITDA Rs1,551 cr, PAT Rs970 cr incl. Rs259 cr net exceptional income). One segment ('core') so that bull/bear deltas flow through the engine's SOTP scenarios. Core and ARACT values are computed in tools/authoring/ARE&M.ctx.js and written here by ARE&M.val.js, which also writes the built other income and finance cost.

segments.name: Lead-acid batteries and allied products (standalone Amara Raja)
segments._why: Revenue = sum of three business lines (assumptions.build, checked in ARE&M.ctx.js). FY27E +14.6%: Q1FY27 +20.6% (OEM 4W +24%, 2W +35%, aftermarket ~+15%, home energy +60%), price increases of ~3% in June and 2-3% in August, a normal Q2 base (Q2FY26 +8%), then the post-GST OEM base from Q3; automotive exports (−20% in Q1) and telecom lead-acid stay weak; lithium pack trading moves to ARACT from Q2. FY28-29E ~9%: management's 9-10% medium-term volume growth for lead-acid (Q1FY27 call), replacement demand from the FY26-27 OEM surge, exports recovering, industrial ex-telecom (UPS, data centres) growing. Street FY27E: MOFSL Rs15,526 cr, Nuvama Rs15,628 cr, Anand Rathi Rs15,409 cr, 360 ONE Rs15,975 cr.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener standalone basis): FY24 14.4%, FY25 13.2%, FY26 11.4%, Q1FY27 10.1% (−140bp YoY: ~0.9pp strategic spending on brand, the Amaron Assist pilot and debottlenecking, plus alloy, sulphuric acid and plastics costs, warranty provisions and freight). FY27E 10.8%: price increases of ~3% (June) and 2-3% (August) catch up with costs, B2B with a lag; strategic spending normalises 'over the next couple of quarters'; traded tubular batteries fall as the own plant meets demand. FY28-29E 11.6-12.0%: operating leverage on ~9% growth and less trading; below management's 13-14% aim, which has no date. Street FY27/28E: MOFSL 10.7/11.8%, Nuvama 11.3/11.5%, Anand Rathi 10.7/12.1%, 360 ONE 11.5/12.9%.

_capexWhy: Lead-acid capex: ~Rs400 cr in FY27 (of the ~Rs1,700 cr group plan, ~Rs1,300 cr is New Energy in ARACT; Q1FY27 call); FY26 ~Rs600 cr gross, ~Rs500 cr net of insurance (Q4FY26 call). FY28-29E Rs450-500 cr: debottlenecking 4W/2W capacity ('more throughput in the same four walls') and the tubular plant. ARACT capex is funded by equity infusions (build.aract.infusion), not here.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs548 cr; Q1FY27 Rs140 cr (run-rate ~Rs560 cr). The rate on average gross block is set so FY27E depreciation is ~Rs570 cr. CWIP is held flat by the engine.
_treasuryWhy: Set to zero: the engine's 'treasury' includes the investments in subsidiaries at cost (ARACT, ARCSPL, ARPSL: Rs2,234 cr at Mar-26), which earn no interest. Interest on liquid funds and on borrowings is built in ARE&M.ctx.js and written into otherIncome and interest.
_otherIncomeWhy: Built (ARE&M.ctx.js checks it): foreign-exchange gains Rs30 cr (FY26 Rs42.8 cr, FY25 Rs38.2 cr; exports ~12% of revenue, not forecast at the FY26 level) + scrap sales Rs12 cr (FY26 Rs12.5 cr) + interest on the Rs120 cr loans to ARPSL and other deposits Rs9 cr (FY26 Rs4.0 cr, loans given during FY26) + other items Rs22 cr (FY26 Rs28.6 cr incl. write-backs) + 7% on positive net liquid funds after ARACT infusions. FY26 normal other income Rs91.9 cr (AR FY26 note 23, before Rs259 cr exceptional income that Screener adds to other income); TTM to Jun-2026 Rs88 cr (Screener 'other income normal'); FY27E is lower because mutual-fund gains (Rs8 cr) go with the cash and FX gains are not assumed to repeat in full.
_interestLabel: Finance cost (warranty unwinding, leases, working-capital debt)
_interestWhy: Built: unwinding of discount on warranty provisions Rs17 cr + lease interest Rs10 cr (FY26 Rs16.8 + 10.0 cr, AR FY26 note 26) + 7.5% on average net borrowings (FY26 'others' Rs13.9 cr on average borrowings of ~Rs210 cr). The parent had net debt of Rs156 cr at Mar-26 (borrowings Rs271 cr, cash Rs115 cr) and borrows to fund ARACT in FY27.
_taxWhy: New regime (25.17%) plus disallowances: FY26 effective ~25.8%, Q1FY27 25.5%.
_payoutWhy: DPS Rs10.6 for FY26 = 20% of EPS (Rs194 cr); 20% in FY24-26 (Screener; AR FY26).

build._why: Automotive (OEM Rs1,800 cr + aftermarket, home energy and auto exports Rs8,399 cr in FY26, Nuvama): Q1FY27 domestic auto +20%+, home energy +60%, exports −20%; H2 against the post-GST OEM base. Industrial (Rs3,018 cr: telecom, UPS and data centres, railways, power, solar, industrial exports): +2% in Q1FY27 as UPS (+10% volume) offsets telecom moving to lithium; Nuvama models +2%/+4%. Others (Rs332 cr: lubes Rs205.5 cr, services, export incentives and scrap): lubes ~Rs50 cr a quarter and growing.

aract._infusionWhy: FY27E: brings the investment in ARACT from Rs1,500 cr (Mar-26) to the ~Rs2,500 cr 'initial risk capital' management says completes the five facilities (Q1FY27 call); Rs400 cr was already in by Aug-2026. FY28-29E: none in the core cash path; further cell capacity is not approved and is excluded (a risk, see the report).
aract._lossWhy: GAM estimates (no company guidance; brokers publish only NPVs). FY26 ARACT loss Rs73 cr (Rs98 cr before tax; AOC-1) on Rs787 cr of pack revenue; consolidated less standalone profit −Rs12 cr in Q1FY27. FY27E: cell R&D of Rs100-150 cr (Q1FY27 call), BESS start-up from Q3FY27 (5-8% operating margin guided). FY28E: the 2 GWh cell line starts (Q2-CY2027) with depreciation and low utilisation. FY29E: BESS at ~5 GWh and better cell utilisation narrow the loss; breakeven FY30E. Bull: BESS ramps fast, breakeven FY30E with smaller losses. Bear: cell approvals lag, breakeven only after FY30E.

dcf._betaWhy: Lead-acid battery maker with near-zero leverage and lead-price pass-through: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5% (same as Exide).
dcf._tgWhy: Batteries track the vehicle parc, power back-up and industrial capex: ~5.5% nominal long-run growth (house range 5-6%), below nominal GDP as telecom, e-rickshaw and EV traction move to lithium.
dcf._fadeWhy: Growth fades from ~9% to 7%; margin 12.5% (between FY26's 11.4% and management's 13-14% aim); capex 3.5% of sales (FY27-29E 2.6-2.7% plus periodic capacity steps); depreciation 3.3% of sales (FY26 4.0%).
dcf._netCashWhy: The engine adds 'treasury' at FY27E: net liquid funds plus the investments in subsidiaries at cost. So the DCF is a core DCF plus ARACT and the other subsidiaries at cost, a cross-check only.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: OEM demand and the replacement wave keep lead-acid volumes growing double digit, price increases stick and trading falls, so margin reaches ~12.5% by FY29E; ARACT's BESS plant fills fast and losses shrink (breakeven FY30E).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Auto-OEM growth reverses against the post-GST base, alloy, acid and plastic costs outrun prices (margin ~11%), exports stay weak and telecom moves to lithium faster; ARACT's cells are not approved on time, losses last beyond FY30E and the market values the subsidiary at half of book.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values Amara Raja: P/E on standalone (lead-acid) FY28E EPS plus the New Energy subsidiary separately at invested capital, book, P/B or NPV (MOFSL, Nuvama, Anand Rathi, ICICI Direct, Avendus).

methods.name: P/E on standalone EPS
methods.why: One multiple on all standalone EPS, with the subsidiaries left to the multiple (as 360 ONE does): shows what the parts add.

methods.name: DCF (core + subsidiaries at cost)
methods.why: Ten-year FCFF of the standalone business at a 12.5% cost of equity, plus net liquid funds and the subsidiaries at cost.
